faqs.q: How much does a Tibetan Spaniel cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $500–$2,000 for a Tibetan Spaniel puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Tibetan Spaniel?
faqs.a: Budget $120–$200 per month for a Tibetan Spaniel, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Small breeds often cost less on food and some products, but vet bills don't proportionally reduce — procedures cost similar amounts regardless of size.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Tibetan Spaniel?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($300–600), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Tibetan Spaniel cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Tibetan Spaniel are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $1,500–$3,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Tibetan Spaniel?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels need brushing 3–5 times per week, daily during seasonal coat blows. The dense undercoat requires a dedicated undercoat rake, not just a surface slicker brush. Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Tibetan Spaniels shed a lot?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels have seasonal shedding — manageable with a consistent brushing routine.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Tibetan Spaniel need?
faqs.a: A slicker brush for surface debris and an undercoat rake for the dense undercoat are both essential. A shedding blade or deshedding tool helps during heavy moult periods. A nail grinder is useful if your Tibetan Spaniel is sensitive to clippers.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Tibetan Spaniel?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Tibetan Spaniels that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Tibetan Spaniels easy to train?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels are considered easier to train than average — they respond quickly to reward-based methods and generalise cues well. Short 10–15 minute sessions outperform long correction-heavy drills.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Tibetan Spaniel?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Tibetan Spaniels. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Tibetan Spaniel?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Tibetan Spaniel?
faqs.a: Most Tibetan Spaniels learn basic obedience cues (sit, stay, come, down) within 2–4 weeks of daily practice. Reliable recall in distracting environments typically takes 2–3 months of consistent reinforcement.

faqs.q: What health problems do Tibetan Spaniels commonly have?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels are most commonly associated with brachycephalic airway issues. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Tibetan Spaniels live?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels have an average lifespan of 12–15 years. Small breeds often live longer than large breeds. Dental care is particularly important for small dogs, as dental disease is a common longevity issue.

faqs.q: Are Tibetan Spaniels prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Tibetan Spaniel puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Tibetan Spaniel puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Tibetan Spaniel-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Tibetan Spaniels good with kids?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels can do well with children when properly socialised from puppyhood. Every dog is an individual — early exposure to children's behaviour (noise, sudden movements) is the most effective preparation.

faqs.q: Do Tibetan Spaniels get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels are generally sociable with other dogs, particularly when well-socialised from puppyhood. Introduce new dogs on neutral territory and keep initial meetings brief and positive.

faqs.q: Do Tibetan Spaniels bark a lot?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels are not considered excessive barkers. They may alert to strangers or unusual sounds, but are generally manageable with basic training. Consistent "quiet" reinforcement from puppyhood keeps this in check.

faqs.q: Are Tibetan Spaniels good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels adapt reasonably well to apartment living, particularly if they receive consistent daily walks and indoor enrichment. Their calm nature makes them less disruptive in confined spaces than high-energy large breeds.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Tibetan Spaniel need per day?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels need approximately 30–45 minutes of exercise daily. A structured morning walk and an evening sniff walk usually cover their needs. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Tibetan Spaniels good running partners?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels are lower-energy dogs and are better suited to brisk walks or short jogs than distance running. Long runs can cause joint strain in lower-activity breeds — stick to 20–30 minute jogs rather than endurance runs.

faqs.q: What happens if a Tibetan Spaniel doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels are less demanding than high-energy breeds, but chronic under-exercise still leads to weight gain and low-level restlessness. Even lower-energy breeds benefit from a consistent daily walk for both physical health and mental stimulation.

faqs.q: Can a Tibetan Spaniel be off-lead?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels can be off-lead in secure areas once recall is reliable. Reliable recall typically takes 3–4 months of consistent training with progressive distance and distractions. Never trust off-lead recall in an unfenced area until it's been tested in controlled conditions first.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Tibetan Spaniel?
faqs.a: A Tibetan Spaniel needs approximately ½–1½ cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Tibetan Spaniel?
faqs.a: Adult Tibetan Spaniels should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Tibetan Spaniel?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Lower-energy Tibetan Spaniels are prone to weight gain — choose a formula with controlled fat content and avoid calorie-dense performance formulas.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Tibetan Spaniel from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Small breeds typically transition to adult food around 12 months. Moving too late keeps them on higher-calorie puppy formulas that can cause weight gain in lower-activity adults.

faqs.q: Is a Tibetan Spaniel a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels are generally considered suitable for first-time owners. They're responsive to training, manageable in size, and adaptable to different home environments. A puppy class is still recommended to build a strong foundation.

faqs.q: Are Tibetan Spaniels good family dogs?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels can be good family dogs when properly socialised. Their suitability depends more on individual temperament and upbringing than breed alone.

faqs.q: Do Tibetan Spaniels do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Tibetan Spaniels form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Tibetan Spaniel?
faqs.a: Plan for 1–1.5 hours per day dedicated to your Tibetan Spaniel — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
